references.text: Nathan told David a parable to expose his sin, in a similar way that Jesus here uses a parable to reveal Simon's wrong attitude toward the sinful woman.
Jesus uses questions and parables in conversation with religious leaders to lead them to recognition, as he here addresses Simon with a parable.
The context of Jesus' address to Simon – Simon the Pharisee had invited Jesus and reacted inwardly to the woman who anointed Jesus' feet.
The following parable that Jesus told Simon about the two debtors is the very content of what Jesus wanted to say to him.
The title 'Rabbi' (Teacher/Didáskalos) is used for Jesus, as Simon here calls him 'Teacher' (Διδάσκαλε), showing that Simon recognized Jesus as a teacher.
The parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector in the temple has a similar theme: the self-righteous compared to one who knows he needs grace, just as Simon is set against the sinful woman here.
Jesus is referred to as 'Teacher' (Διδάσκαλε), a title used by many who addressed him, including Pharisees like Simon here.
